pr_title: Fix:- Fixed dev tools inspect mode on Shadow dom
pr_body:
Fixes #26200 

### PR explanation

I tried to induce the change by the `event.composed` to check whether the event was created in a  ShadowRoot, And replaced `pointerOver` with `pointerMove`,  pointerOver event did not fired correctly

https://github.com/facebook/react/assets/72331432/9f986ff2-785f-4cba-a504-44f82ea9fc5a

review_comments: Any particular reason why to use `pointermove` over `pointerover`?

@hoxyq  I used `pointermove` instead of `pointerover` since we need to get the latest element which we would be hovering on,
taking the example say we have a dom hierarchy 

```
<div-root>
    shadow-root
    <div x>
   <div y>
```

When we hover on div-x, pointerover will fire on div-root because div-x is inside a ShadowRoot, then,
when the hover target changed to div-y, no new pointerover event will be fired because the hover target is still inside the same ShadowRoot.

The last time I debugged it, `pointerover` was emitted each time when I hovered over some element inside shadow-root with mode = open.

I will double-check that tomorrow and return with more feedback

Yes, in case when multiple components are inside shadow root, hovering over them will not fire multiple `pointerover` events.

Overall, looks good to me, thanks for working on this. I will leave 1 small comment, can merge after this changed
If we could listen to `pointerover` event, do we need this kind of optimization? Or what is the purpose of it?

this basically check if the target node  is the same as the lasthoverednode and if it is , then we are doing an early return for the same, this can help us to prevent extra dom calculations happening on it if the hovered node has not changed!
@hoxyq the return types were any earlier so should not be an issue!
